:::{#thm-reduction-preserves-p}
#### Reductions carry polynomial-time algorithms back

If $L \le_p L'$ (@def-reduction) and $L'$ is in
[P](p-and-np.qmd#def-class-p), then $L$ is in P.

:::

::: {.proof}

Let $f$ be the reduction.
A big-O bound holds from some $n_0$ on,
and raising its constant to cover the finitely many lengths below $n_0$
turns it into a bound for every length.
So there are constants $a, b \ge 1$ and $c, d \ge 0$ such that,
on inputs of every length $n \ge 0$,
computing $f$ takes at most $a (n + 1)^{c}$ steps,
and some algorithm decides $L'$ within $b (n + 1)^{d}$ steps.

On input $x$ of length $n$, compute $f(x)$ and then decide whether $f(x) \in L'$.
The answer is correct because $x \in L$ exactly when $f(x) \in L'$.

Each step writes at most some fixed number $k$ of output bits,
so $|f(x)| \le k a (n + 1)^{c}$.
Since $(n + 1)^{c} \ge 1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|f(x)| + 1
&\le k a (n + 1)^{c} + 1 \\
&\le (k a + 1) (n + 1)^{c}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The two stages together take at most

$$
\begin{aligned}
a (n + 1)^{c} + b \paren{|f(x)| + 1}^{d}
&\le a (n + 1)^{c} + b \sb{(k a + 1) (n + 1)^{c}}^{d} \\
&= a (n + 1)^{c} + b (k a + 1)^{d} (n + 1)^{cd}
\end{aligned}
$$

steps, which is $O(n^{\max(c, cd)})$, a polynomial bound.

:::
